title: A simultaneous graded tail rank condition defines an immersion
statement: Let $U$ be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}\mathcal A_d$ be a quasi-coherent graded commutative $\mathcal O_U$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures, pqf-def-coherent] with $\mathcal A_0=\mathcal O_U$, generated by a coherent $\mathcal A_1$. Let $M=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}M_d$ be a finitely generated graded $\mathcal A$-module, with quasi-coherent homogeneous pieces. Fix $m\geq0$ and $P\in\mathbf Q[t]$ with $P(d)\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ for every integer $d\geq m$. There is an immersion $j:U_{M,P,m}\to U$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], unique as a subfunctor of the functor of points of $U$, such that for every morphism $g:T\to U$ from an arbitrary scheme $T$, $g$ factors through $j$ if and only if $g^*M_d$ is locally free of rank $P(d)$ for every $d\geq m$. Locally free of rank $r$ means locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_T^{\oplus r}$, and $g^*$ is ordinary module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. The immersion is of finite type. The base-changed immersion over any $U'\to U$ has the same universal rank-condition property for the pulled-back pieces, even when $U'$ is not Noetherian.

source.place: Grothendieck, Bourbaki Expose 221, Lemma 3.4 and proof using Lemmas 3.5--3.6, printed pp.262--264. Archival PDF WANTED; primary PDF read online.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-graded-fibre-hilbert-functions-finite] to $(\mathcal A,M)$ over $U$. Its hypotheses are exactly the Noetherian, degree-one finite generation, and finite graded generation hypotheses here. Thus every $M_d$ is coherent and the functions $h_u(d)=\dim_{\kappa(u)}(M_{d,u}\otimes\kappa(u))$ lie in a finite set $H$. No flatness of $M$ over $U$ is being assumed.

Apply [lem-sfb-finite-profile-rank-open] with $F_d=M_d$ and $r_d=P(d)$ for $d\geq m$. Step 1 supplies coherent pieces and the finite set $H$; the hypothesis on $P$ supplies nonnegative integral ranks. Obtain the Noetherian open $V\subseteq U$ and the closed loci $C_d\hookrightarrow V$ with ideals $\mathcal I_d$. Every map satisfying all rank conditions factors uniquely through $V$, and over $V$ the degree-$d$ condition is equivalent to factorization through $C_d$.

source.place: Lemmas 3.5--3.6: finite upper-rank tests and closed individual rank equations

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-noetherian-closed-family-intersection] to $V\subseteq U$ and $(\mathcal I_d)_{d\geq m}$. It gives $Z\hookrightarrow V$ with ideal $\sum_d\mathcal I_d$, stabilized in finitely many degrees, and a finite-type immersion $j:Z\to U$. If $g:T\to U$ satisfies all ranks, Step 2 gives its unique lift $t:T\to V$. For this lift, every degree condition is equivalent to factorization through $C_d$. The cited intersection property gives a unique lift through $Z$. Conversely a lift through $Z$ induces a lift through every $C_d$, hence all ranks. Uniqueness through $V$ and through $Z\hookrightarrow V$ gives uniqueness through $j$ for every $T$.

source.place: Lemma 3.4 after Lemma 3.6: stationary closed intersection and arbitrary-test-scheme property

proof.text: Every test scheme has at most one factorization through $j$, as shown by the quotient-ring and open-subscheme descriptions in Step 3. Hence its image on functors of points is exactly the specified rank subfunctor. Any two such representing immersions have a unique compatible isomorphism by [lem-pc-representable-unique], which proves uniqueness as a subfunctor.

For any $U\prime\to U$, form $Z\prime=Z\times_UU\prime$. The base-changed closed part is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]; the open part is the inverse image open $V\prime\subseteq U\prime$. Thus $Z\prime\to U\prime$ is an immersion. For $t:T\to U\prime$, the fibre-product universal property bijects its lifts through $Z\prime$ with lifts of $g:T\to U$, its composite, through $Z$. Thus existence and uniqueness of lifts are preserved. By Step 3 this is equivalent to $g^*M_d$ being locally free of rank $P(d)$ for every $d\geq m$. The composition isomorphism of [def-pc-module-pullback] identifies this with the pullback along $t$ of the pieces pulled back to $U\prime$. This proves the asserted property without applying any Noetherian theorem over $U\prime$.

source.place: Lemma 3.4, arbitrary test schemes, and base change of the representing subfunctor

lean.statement: theorem exists_gradedTailRankStratum (U : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian U] (B K : ℕ → U.Modules) (A : GradedSheafAlgebra B) (M : GradedSheafModule A K) (hB : ∀ d : ℕ, SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent.{u} (B d)) (hzero : IsIso A.unit) (hone : RingedSpace.IsCoherent U.toRingedSpace (B 1)) (hgen : A.IsGeneratedInDegreeOne) (hK : ∀ d : ℕ, SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent.{u} (K d)) (hM : M.IsLocallyFinitelyGenerated) (m : ℕ) (P : Polynomial ℚ) (hP : ∀ d : ℕ, m ≤ d → ∃ r : ℕ, P.eval (d : ℚ) = (r : ℚ)) : ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (j : Z ⟶ U), IsImmersion j ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType j ∧ QuasiCompact j ∧ (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : T ⟶ U), (∃! h : T ⟶ Z, h ≫ j = g) ↔ gradedTailRankCondition K P m g) ∧ (∀ (Z' : Scheme.{u}) (j' : Z' ⟶ U), IsImmersion j' → (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : T ⟶ U), (∃ h : T ⟶ Z', h ≫ j' = g) ↔ gradedTailRankCondition K P m g) → ∃! e : Z ≅ Z', e.hom ≫ j' = j) ∧ (∀ (U' : Scheme.{u}) (b : U' ⟶ U), IsImmersion (pullback.snd j b) ∧ ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (t : T ⟶ U'), (∃! h : T ⟶ pullback j b, h ≫ pullback.snd j b = t) ↔ gradedTailRankCondition (fun d : ℕ ↦ (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback b).obj (K d)) P m t)
